editorial:
Ever wondered what would happen if the old Jekyll and Hyde story took place in the modern world with a female lead? You get to see that here. You meet Nina, a lonely doctor who stays inside her house and hides a dark secret. When she hires Rob to help her around the place, things start off sweet and simple. But you quickly realize that Nina isn't just shy. She has another personality named Hyde who is mean, scary, and wants to take over completely. The vibe is tense and creepy, making you feel like something bad is about to happen every time the camera moves.

The acting is the best part because the lead actress does a great job switching between the two personalities. You will love the twists, though some parts of the story move a bit slow in the middle. If you like psychological thrillers that mess with your head, you should definitely check this out. It looks great in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video if you want to see every detail, or you can just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. Adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is also a smart move if you love owning your movies.
endingExplained: At the end, you find out that Hyde is not just a mood swing, but a full person living inside Nina. Nina tries to use medicine to stop Hyde for good, but Hyde is too strong. In the final scenes, Hyde completely wins the fight for control of the body. Nina disappears for good, and Hyde takes over her life entirely. It ends on a dark note because the evil side wins and there is no way to bring the real Nina back.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological twists and modern retellings of classic stories.
